picks.style: vedic hymn, tanpura drone, deep male voice, slow, reverent, sparse
picks.why: The opening hymn of the Rigveda — Agni praised at dusk and dawn, the first words of the tradition.

picks.style: riddle chant, tanpura and low frame drum, hushed male voice, slow, enigmatic
picks.why: The Riddle Hymn: seven-wheeled chariot, seven sisters, 'Childlike I ask, not knowing in my mind.'

picks.style: vedic praise hymn with refrain, drone and hand-struck drum, strong male voice, building, emphatic
picks.why: Built on the great refrain — he who stilled the mountains, who propped up the sky, 'he, O people, is Indra.'

picks.style: baroque seduction aria, harpsichord and viol, honeyed soprano, languid, coaxing
picks.why: Sloth's whole seduction speech: 'Rough is the road to fame, thro' blood and war; smooth is my way, and all my paths are peace.'

picks.style: allegorical art song, chamber strings and oboe, clear tenor, stately, expectant
picks.why: The two enormous women appearing on the road to the young Hercules — one striking awe, one winning love.

picks.style: english country ballad, fiddle and cittern, bright male voice with chorus, brisk, roguish
picks.why: A genuine ballad with a returning refrain — 'away to the Link' and 'a cool walk on the Link'.

picks.style: pastoral octosyllabic song, acoustic guitar and recorder, warm tenor, unhurried, reflective
picks.why: Dyer's most quoted lines — 'a little rule, a little sway... between the cradle and the grave' — and the rivers running to endless sleep.

picks.style: anapaestic country air, fiddle and hand drum, easy baritone, swinging, good-humoured
picks.why: Already a song rhythm: 'Have my friends in the town, in the gay busy town, forgot such a man as John Dyer?'

picks.style: ruins elegy, low strings and distant horn, grave male voice, slow, hollow
picks.why: The monk over the tombs where 'Caesars, heroes, peasants, hermits lie, blended in dust together'.

picks.style: georgian canzonetta, fortepiano and cello, tender soprano, gentle, aching
picks.why: A finished song with a returning refrain: 'No more I'll murmur and complain, for thou, my love, wilt think on me.'

picks.style: mad song, harp and sparse strings, unsteady female voice, shifting tempo, haunted
picks.why: The Maniac's Song — 'I had a friend, she prov'd unkind; I had a love, he prov'd untrue' — and a passing bell.

picks.style: funeral dirge, string quartet and soft voices, clear female lead, slow, processional
picks.why: Rosemary, rue, virgin lilies and wild rose strewn on a grave — a dirge already written for singers.

picks.style: morning pastoral ballad, fiddle and flute, bright female vocal, lively, fresh
picks.why: 'Awake, my fair, the morning springs' — the heifer lows, the blackbird sings; ballad metre made for singing.

picks.style: satirical parlour song, harpsichord and pizzicato strings, arch baritone, brisk, cutting
picks.why: Witwoud young against Witwoud old, closing on flies that grow blind and sting us at the last.

picks.style: garden fable air, lute and recorder, light tenor, courtly, playful
picks.why: The tall tulip lording it over the lily of the valley — the fable set up in one clean scene.

picks.style: greek invective song, lyre and hard-struck drum, biting male voice, driving, sardonic
picks.why: Timocreon's attack song in full — three talents of silver, stale meats, and guests praying against their host.

picks.style: greek satirical air, kithara and light percussion, wry male voice, moderate, mocking
picks.why: The Andrians answering Persuasion and Compulsion with their own two gods, Penury and Powerlessness.

picks.style: greek toast song, lyre and hand drum, warm male voice, easy, convivial
picks.why: Only candidate; a chain of greetings ending in a drinking-toast order — health first, then prosperity, then joy.

picks.style: greek epitaph chant, single lyre, unaccompanied male voice, sparse, final
picks.why: Only candidate; short but complete — 'the games are done, the crowns all won; no more delay.'
